title: How well does a small maritime segmentation network find floating obstacles, and what do fog and sun glint cost? MaSTr1325 on a CPU
lede: an LR-ASPP MobileNetV3 trained on MaSTr1325 scores 0.97 mIoU on held-out sequences yet finds only 35% of 80 floating obstacles (62% of those of 16 px or more); uniform fog at transmission 0.15 cuts the clean-trained net's large-object recall to 23% (wide seed spread), fog-and-glint augmentation holds it at 62% (same fog model), and glint raises false alarms on open water 4.6x for the clean-trained net
summary: Milestone 9a of track 23 (marine-detect), filed under the marine-hull programme. Public MaSTr1325 data (Bovcon et al. 2019, CC BY 4.0), split by blocks of 25 consecutive frames to avoid near-duplicate leakage (1025 train, 300 test), at 320×240 on 4 CPU cores. Models: LR-ASPP on an ImageNet MobileNetV3-Large backbone, trained clean and with fog plus glint augmentation, and a per-pixel colour-and-row MLP; 3 seeds each. Beyond pixel IoU, a MODS-style detection score from the masks: a floating obstacle (an 8-connected obstacle component of at least 4 px, ringed by water, not touching the frame) is found when half its pixels are predicted obstacle; a false alarm is a predicted blob of 4+ px wholly on water. Fog is the Koschmieder scattering model with uniform transmission; glint is stylised saturating highlights with swept strength (no sourced glint statistics). Result (re-scored 2026-11-18 after a quality audit found 4-connected, no-floor counting that split thin structures into 1-px objects): mIoU 0.967 but 35% of 80 floating obstacles found (48 are 4–15 px, found 15–17%; 32 larger ones, 62–65%); fog at t = 0.15 cuts the clean net's large-object recall to 23% (±60 over seeds) while mIoU stays 0.88; augmentation keeps it at 62–66% on the same fog model; glint raises the clean net's false alarms from 0.06 to 0.27 per frame and leaves recall flat. Preliminary: reduced resolution, no IMU channel, not a reproduction of WaSR or the MODS protocol, one harbour in fair weather, uniform fog. Research code, not a certified perception system.
